title: Prune GraphQL field overfetch and introduce tiered cache segmentation for Console backend
creator: Liam Wong
description:
Background: The Console backend has accumulated multiple small GraphQL resolvers that request broad field fragments from core services. This has resulted in repeated overfetching, higher serialization cost, and noisy cache keys in the existing in-memory and Redis caching layers. Previous efforts focused on cache coalescing and request coalescing but did not address field-level payload bloat or cross-layer cache segmentation.

Goal: Reduce tail latency and CPU overhead on Console API by (1) eliminating common overfetch patterns at the GraphQL layer, (2) implementing a lightweight field-aware cache segmentation strategy (hot-object vs. metadata tiers), and (3) introducing small resolver-level mini-batching for nodes with many child fetches. Target is 10-15% p95 latency reduction on Console list/detail endpoints and 20-30% reduction in bytes transferred between services under median load.

Proposed work:
- Audit top-20 Console GraphQL queries (by volume and latency) and produce a minimized fragment map that only requests required fields per route.
- Add a resolver-side 'field-hint' mechanism: resolvers report the set of requested top-level fields so downstream service clients can choose narrow projections.
- Implement tiered cache segmentation: introduce two cache namespaces in Redis and local memory: "hot" (full object, high TTL, LRU-friendly) and "meta" (small metadata fragments, short TTL). Canonicalization rules and keys documented in the design doc.
- Add a compact cache stamp to responses (short hash + version) to validate cross-node coherency and support safe stale-while-revalidate on cache misses.
- Introduce mini-batching for children fetches in the resolver that currently fan out to many single-key requests (combine into chunked multi-get/multi-call where supported).
- Remove legacy serializer layers that materialize full objects for routes that only need a small subset; replace with projection-aware serializers.

Implementation steps: (1) Audit and fragment-map (2 weeks) -> produce mapping PR and tests. (2) Field-hint API and client changes (1 week) -> feature-flagged. (3) Tiered cache prototype in staging (2 weeks) -> run perf benchmarks. (4) Mini-batching + serializers cleanup (1.5 weeks) -> integration tests. (5) Progressive rollout behind feature flag and A/B test to measure real improvements.

Acceptance criteria:
- PRs merged for fragment map, field-hint, and tiered cache with unit + integration tests.
- p95 latency for Console list/detail endpoints reduced by >=10% in staging perf runs and validated in canary rollout.
- Redis network bandwidth for Console keys reduced by >=15% on median traffic patterns.
- No increased error rate or cache incoherency incidents during a 2-week canary (monitoring: 5xx, cache miss rate, cache stamp mismatch).

Rollout plan: Feature-flag everything. Enable in staging cluster then canary 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor metrics and tracing. If stable, escalate to 25% then 100% over 5 days. If cache stamp mismatches exceed threshold, auto-roll-back.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Field-hint changes require downstream schema/backwards compatibility. Mitigation: Field-hint defaults to full projection, opt-in via header and gradual client rollout.
- Risk: Two-tier cache adds operational complexity. Mitigation: Start with conservative TTLs and add dashboards for hit/miss per tier; add automated rebalancing playbook.
- Risk: Mini-batching could change request distribution and overload target services. Mitigation: Rate-limit batches, maintain chunk-size config, and coordinate with dependent service owners during rollout.

References and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CI/Field-aware+cache+and+fragment+audit (internal).
- Perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console-backend/perf (staging).
- WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1429 (fragment map).

Notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to infrastructure and wiring changes; no UX changes. Follow-on work may consider query plan caching in Gateway for broader multi-service optimizations.

2026-01-18 - Eng Review: Raised concern about cache stamp size; switched to short 8-byte hash to reduce key bloat. Decision logged in design doc.
